preconditioning with brief intermittent ischemia lessened the detrimental effects of subsequent sustained ischemia, and that the beneficial effects were not blocked by BW-A1433, CPDPX, or 8-sulfophenyltheophylline, but were blocked by PD-115, 199.

the mechanism of preconditioning in the heart.
the role of adenosine in preconditioning and its effect on anaerobic glycosis during ischemia.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adenosine antagonism does not block preconditioning in the isolated rat heart, but that the effects may be dependent on the type of adenosine antagonist used.
adenosine antagonism with CPDPX does not block the effect of ischemic preconditioning on 31P-NMR-detectable metabolic changes during sustained ischemia or on functional recovery on reflow.
adenosine antagonism is not a universal phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

adenosine antagonism does not block the effect of ischemic preconditioning in the rat heart, and that CPDPX, which blocks adenosine receptors but does not block glucose uptake, is not a useful tool for studying preconditioning.
adenosine antagonism does not reverse preconditioning and that the mechanism of preconditioning does not involve adenosine-mediated inhibition of anaerobic glycosis.
adenosine is not the only mediator of preconditioning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adenosine is not the mediator of preconditioned protection.

the effect of preconditioned on the ionic changes during sustained ischemia does not require adenosine receptors, whereas the beneficial effects of preconditioning on recovery of function are adenosine receptor mediated.
the adenosine antagonistic properties of BW-A143 3U are not the reason that preconditioning is blocked by BW-A1433.
